instruction.text: Which two words describe people’s experience of the fire?

feedback.end: The Great Fire of London was a horrible experience for the people involved.

instruction.text: Select the total deaths on the official records of the fire to find out more.

feedback.end: The official records show that only 6 people died in the fire. However, some historians think that hundreds were probably killed. Many people were sadly just never found.

atoms.b: The records also show that the fire destroyed around 13,200 ((++houses televisions)), 87 churches and even the old St Paul’s Cathedral!
Thousands of people were left ((happy ++homeless)). Many of them died from being out in the cold for too long.
Camps were set up on the edge of the city for the homeless so they had somewhere to ((swim ++stay)) until houses were rebuilt.

instruction.text: You’re talking to King Charles II about his plan to rebuild London. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: How did you plan to ((replay ++rebuild)) London?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.5st'>How did you plan to rebuild London?</prosody>

atoms.b: I knew I couldn’t plan the rebuilding of London on my own, so I worked with ((bakers ++architects)) to design the new city.
Where did you get the ((++money eggs)) from to do this?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.5st'>Where did you get the money from to do this?</prosody>

atoms.b: I set up a relief fund so that people could ((++donate sing)) money to help.
How did you make sure that another ((concert ++fire)) wouldn’t happen again?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.5st'>How did you make sure that another fire wouldn’t happen again?</prosody>

atoms.b: I put in a set of ((songs ++rules)) for all future construction.

instruction.text: Do you think these rules were put in place by King Charles II after the fire?

atoms.a: all buildings should be made of chocolate
all businesses using fire must be built in one area

feedback.finish: After these changes, buildings were less flammable and fires spread less quickly. Living conditions for most people in London also majorly improved.
